newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jiangxi Copper 1996 pretax profits $48.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: China Jiangxi Copper 1996 pretax profits $48.2 mln.

text.p: China's Jiangxi Copper Co realised a pretax profit of 400 million yuan ($48.2 million) in 1996, a company official said on Thursday.
Slumping world copper prices last year had cut into Jiangxi Copper's expected earnings, company spokesman Ma Ping said by telephone, but did not elaborate. He did not say what post-tax profits were.
The company, one of China's largest copper producers, turned out 303,000 tonnes of copper last year, Ma said.
Of that, 202,000 tonnes was electrolytic copper and 101,000 was copper refined directly from ore, Ma said.
The firm also produced 431,000 tonnes of sulphuric acid, nearly 5.0 tonnes of gold and 84.0 tonnes of silver, Ma said.
Jiangxi Copper was among 38 firms approved last Sunday for listing their shares on stock markets abroad.
Earlier reports quoted company president He Changming as saying the firm hoped to raise $200 million through a share flotation in Hong Kong.
